settings.name_in_paper: Online RL algorithm selection (online off-policy RL AS problem)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Arms are off-policy RL algorithms on an episodic RL task; arm reward distributions evolve with the shared trajectory set collected by the learner (state-dependent, underlying episodic RL).
unmapped: arms are off-policy RL learners whose expected return depends on the trajectory set collected so far (history-dependent, learning arms)
returns are bounded discounted sums of rewards in [R_min, R_max]
Assumptions: more data is better data, order compatibility, learning is fair
settings.definition_quote: given an episodic task and a finite number of off-policy RL algorithms, a meta-algorithm has to decide which RL algorithm is in control during the next episode so as to maximize the expected return.

algorithms.name: ESBAS (Epochal Stochastic Bandit Algorithm Selection) with UCB1

symbols.rho_abs_worst: max over portfolio algorithms of the absolute pseudo-regret of the canonical meta-algorithm always selecting that algorithm, at horizon T

source.label: th:notworse
source.quote: The absolute pseudo-regret is bounded by the worst algorithm absolute pseudo-regret in order of magnitude: \forall \sigma, \overline{\rho}_{abs}^\sigma(T)\in\mathcal{O}\left(\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal{P}} \overline{\rho}_{abs}^{\sigma^\alpha}(T)\right).

results.notes: Holds for every meta-algorithm; the proof gives the explicit bound K * max_alpha rho_abs^{sigma^alpha}(T). Absolute pseudo-regret is measured against the optimal expected return achievable by any portfolio policy.

symbols.G_sum: sum_{beta=0}^{floor(log T)} beta / Delta_beta^dag, where Delta_beta^dag is the smallest nonzero gap between portfolio algorithms' expected returns at epoch beta

conditions: the stochastic bandit Xi used within each epoch guarantees regret O(log(T)/Delta_beta^dag)

source.label: th:shortsightedregret
source.quote: If the stochastic multi-armed bandit $\Xi$ guarantees a regret of order of magnitude $\mathcal{O}(\log(T)/\Delta_\beta^\dag)$, then: \overline{\rho}^{\sigma^{\textsc{esbas}}}_{ss}(T)\in\mathcal{O}\left(\displaystyle\sum_{\beta=0}^{\lfloor \log(T) \rfloor} \cfrac{\beta}{\Delta_\beta^\dag}\right).

results.notes: Short-sighted pseudo-regret: against the best algorithm given the current trajectory set at each meta-time (mapped to best_action_per_round).

symbols.Delta_inf: limit of the smallest nonzero gap between portfolio algorithms as the epoch tends to infinity, mu*_inf - mu^dag_inf > 0

conditions: the stochastic bandit Xi guarantees regret O(log(T)/Delta)

symbols.m_dag: polynomial decay exponent of the smallest gap in the epoch index beta

conditions: the stochastic bandit Xi guarantees regret O(log(T)/Delta)

symbols.c_dag: exponent with Delta_beta^dag in Theta(T^{-c_dag}), 0 < c_dag < 1

conditions: the stochastic bandit Xi guarantees regret O(log(T)/Delta)
results.notes: Short-sighted pseudo-regret of ESBAS. Table 1 also reports O(T^{1-c^dag}) when c^dag >= 0.5 (obtained by summing gaps) and O(log T) for Delta ~ 1/T, but these are not stated as formal results.

symbols.rho_star_3K: absolute pseudo-regret at horizon T/(3K) of the canonical meta-algorithm always selecting the best algorithm alpha* = argmin_alpha rho_abs^{sigma^alpha}(T)
symbols.rho_ss: ESBAS short-sighted pseudo-regret at horizon T

conditions: Assumptions 1 and 2 used in the proof
the stochastic bandit Xi guarantees the best arm is selected at least T/K times in the first T episodes with probability 1 - delta_T, delta_T in O(1/T)

source.label: th:absolute
source.quote: Under assumption \ref{ass:fairlearning}, if the stochastic multi-armed bandit $\Xi$ guarantees that the best arm has been selected in the $T$ first episodes at least $T/K$ times, with high probability $\delta_T \in \mathcal{O}(1/T)$, then: \exists \kappa>0, \forall T\geq 9K^2, \overline{\rho}^{\sigma^{\textsc{esbas}}}_{abs}(T) \leq (3K+1) \overline{\rho}^{\sigma^*}_{abs}\left(\frac{T}{3K}\right) + \overline{\rho}_{ss}^{\sigma^{\textsc{esbas}}}(T) + \kappa\log(T)

results.notes: Absolute pseudo-regret decomposition; kappa is an existential constant.
